rule: Shortlist in its fixed order; at most one question per MR. First 10 MRs with a stated reason = answerable (188 skipped: no reason seen). Next 2 = removed. no_reason picked from later MRs, needs a person's check.

questions.q: Why are job input expressions treated as literal text when a job declares no inputs?
questions.a: Users may already use the same ${{ }} syntax for unrelated reasons, and evaluating it would make those expressions fail, which is a breaking change.
quotes: interpolation syntax (`${{ ... }}`) for an unrelated reason then
those expressions may fail to evaluate.

questions.q: Why does the helper image naming fall back to Linux when no operating system is named?
questions.a: It matches the tag strategy already in use, which the Docker community appears to have standardised on.
quotes: I think it's a good idea to "default" to Linux because looking at the tags strategy we are doing the same

questions.q: Why did integration tests stop reading the token from GITLAB_TOKEN?
questions.a: Many tools use that variable and people often have highly privileged tokens exported under that name, which has led to accidents.
quotes: It's a variable that's used with many toolings, and people often have (too) high-privileged tokens in their shell exported as `GITLAB_TOKEN`.

questions.q: Why was uid:gid syntax added to the Kubernetes executor's user option?
questions.a: To make it consistent with the Docker executor options.
quotes: Bring consistency between Docker and Kubernetes executor options

questions.q: Why did the helper image use Alpine 3.4 when 3.5 was already the current stable release?
questions.a: multiarch/alpine had no 3.5 version for arm, and the old stable was good enough for this use.
quotes: `multiarch/alpine` doesn't have 3.5 version for arm architecture.

questions.q: Why was the runner's runtime state separated from the job status exposed to after_script?
questions.a: Otherwise after_script running on failure made metrics report the job as completed rather than running.
quotes: Having `CI_JOB_STATUS` be equal to the runtime state meant that the newly introduced `after_script` even on failure behaviour would report via metrics that the job was no longer `running`, but instead completed.

questions.q: Why was the message logged when a docker-machine build ends reworded?
questions.a: The old message printed <nil> after success, which people could mistake for a failure.
quotes: Some might mistaken this as a failure.

questions.q: Why is the log prefix no longer passed through secret scrubbing in the build logger?
questions.a: Log prefixes are nearly static and do not contain URL tokens, and a smaller input to the scrubber is better.
quotes: Our log prefixes are pretty much static and won't include URL tokens, and the smaller the input to `ScrubSecrets` the better.

questions.q: Why was the third-party home directory library replaced with code inside the runner?
questions.a: The library deprecated parts of itself, adapting caused a regression, and the code was simple enough to bring in directly.
quotes: on is so simple that we could just bring it to runner's codebase

questions.q: Why should variables be allowed in the cache policy setting?
questions.a: It reduces duplication across jobs, because rules can set the value through a variable.
quotes: It allows reducing duplication in jobs, by leveraging variables (via `rules`) to customize the value of `cache:policy`

questions.q: Why are Git credentials now also set up for nested submodules?
questions.a: To preserve existing workflows that run git submodule update from nested directories.
quotes: To preserve existing workflows, recursively update the nested submodules

questions.q: Why did the hard-coded username in the shell integration tests need to change?
questions.a: The hard-coded username made it impossible to run them locally without a CI job token.
